## Predict the signs before listing pairs

For $x^2+bx+c$, record $P=c$ and $S=b$. The product tells you whether the signs match. The sum tells you which signs to use.

::: {.fragment}

| Product | Sum | Signs of the pair |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Positive | Positive | Both positive. |
| Positive | Negative | Both negative. |
| Negative | Positive | Opposite signs. Give the number farther from zero the positive sign. |
| Negative | Negative | Opposite signs. Give the number farther from zero the negative sign. |

:::

On paper: if $P=-12$ and $S=-1$, which number in the pair must be negative?

::: {.fragment}

The number farther from zero must be negative. With $3$ and $4$, use $3$ and $-4$: their sum is $-1$.

:::
